correctness.rationale: A covered inclusion-minimal codeword is minimal and, under the long-gap condition, must have weight d. Ratio pigeonholing cancels at least ceil(d/(q-1)) coordinates, forcing a second minimum-weight word; the target codeword support then lies in a union of size at most 2d. The explicit [5,2,2]_q counterexample family and finite checks agree with the formulas.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The motivating 2026 preprint proves only the binary mirror theorem and says q-ary extensions need extra conditions; its MDS discussion does not give a same-hypotheses counterexample. Searches over q-ary mirror bands, local weight gaps, vanishing partial weight distributions, minimal-codeword arguments, the source paper and the SCOPE archive found no prior coverage. The source is extremely recent, so near-simultaneous or revision risk remains.

value.rationale: The result both gives an explicit all-q>=3 counterexample under the exact binary-style hypotheses and supplies a positive q-ary replacement with an explicit alphabet-dependent endpoint, clarifying the actual boundary of the newly proposed mirror phenomenon.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
